candidates.zhHeadline: Atlassian AMP：把 Agent 变成团队里的可见协作者
candidates.enHeadline: Atlassian AMP makes agents visible collaborators inside the team workspace
candidates.zhFact: Atlassian 宣布 AMP（Agentic Multiplayer Protocol）开始 rollout，把 Agent 的身份、上下文、权限、归属和审计接进 Jira、Confluence 与 Teamwork Graph。Agent 可以被 @mention、接收 Loom 视频或文档中的选择作为结构化 brief，在 Jira 中处理分流，并把本地 IDE/终端会话桥接回工作项。它是团队协作与治理开发面，不是一个孤立聊天机器人。
candidates.enFact: Atlassian announced rollout of AMP, the Agentic Multiplayer Protocol, connecting agent identity, context, permissions, ownership, and audit to Jira, Confluence, and the Teamwork Graph. An agent can be mentioned, receive a Loom video or document selection as a structured brief, handle triage in Jira, and bridge a local IDE or terminal session back to a work item. It is a team-collaboration and governance developer surface, not an isolated chatbot.
candidates.zhValue: 产品价值在于把 Agent 的工作从个人窗口搬回团队共同查看的空间。人类同事可以看到谁触发了 Agent、它访问了什么、改了哪些内容、由谁负责；本地运行的 coding agent 也不再是 Jira 之外的黑盒。对设计、产品和工程团队，交付物、评论、选择和验收条件可以成为 Agent 的上下文，而不是靠复制粘贴重新解释。
candidates.enValue: The product value is moving agent work from a private window into a space the team can inspect together. Colleagues can see who triggered an agent, what it touched, what it changed, and who owns it; a coding agent running locally is no longer a black box outside Jira. For design, product, and engineering teams, artifacts, comments, selections, and acceptance criteria become agent context instead of material that someone must copy and explain again.
candidates.zhImplication: 验收不该只看 Agent 是否完成 Jira 分流，而要看身份是否清楚、权限是否继承正确、局部选择是否保留语义、Agent 光标和人类光标是否不会互相遮挡，以及 Agent 写回后是否有可读的变更历史。AMP 还把责任链推向界面：服务账号、非人身份、人工 checkpoint 和撤销权限都应该在同一工作面可见。
candidates.enImplication: Acceptance should test more than whether an agent completes Jira triage. Test whether identity is clear, permissions inherit correctly, a local selection preserves meaning, agent and human presence do not collide, and a write-back creates a readable change history. AMP also moves accountability into the interface: service accounts, non-human identities, human checkpoints, and revocation should be visible in the same work surface.

en.productName: Atlassian AMP is the Agentic Multiplayer Protocol announced with the Team ’26 Europe rollout. It treats an agent as a non-human collaborator connecting Jira, Confluence, Loom, IDEs, terminals, and the Teamwork Graph. The public article describes a protocol and platform capability, not a separately sold chatbot. Any price, version, region, interface, battery, success rate, privacy, or delivery detail not disclosed by the cited source remains source not stated; it is not inferred from product imagery or marketing language.
en.productType: The product is a team-agent collaboration and governance developer surface. AMP covers context transfer, agent identity, ownership, real-time presence, permission inheritance, human checkpoints, and activity audit. Rovo, Jira Agent Sessions, the MCP server, and the Teamwork Graph are the work layers where it can land. Users encounter comments, mentions, cursors, work-item state, and change history. Any price, version, region, interface, battery, success rate, privacy, or delivery detail not disclosed by the cited source remains source not stated; it is not inferred from product imagery or marketing language.

The agent reads authorised Teamwork Graph context, acts in the work item or connected tool, and writes back its result, changes, ownership, and audit trail. A local IDE or terminal session can also be bridged into Jira. Any price, version, region, interface, battery, success rate, privacy, or delivery detail not disclosed by the cited source remains source not stated; it is not inferred from product imagery or marketing language.
en.specsOrStack: Atlassian names the Teamwork Graph, Atlassian MCP server, Atlassian CLI, Jira Agent Sessions, Rovo, Artifacts, agent accounts, and a non-human identity inventory. The article also cites seven context types, more than 80 connectors, and 250 billion connected objects; those are company-disclosed scale figures. Cross-vendor protocol details, API version, latency, SLA, billing, and retention are source not stated. Any price, version, region, interface, battery, success rate, privacy, or delivery detail not disclosed by the cited source remains source not stated; it is not inferred from product imagery or marketing language.
en.useCases: Concrete cases include an agent routing Jira work from comments, generating acceptance criteria from a Confluence selection, using a Loom explanation, reading context beside Figma or an IDE, linking a local coding session to the right work item, and assigning different service identities to HR or helpdesk agents. The team sees agent activity in the same surface instead of chasing a private window. Any price, version, region, interface, battery, success rate, privacy, or delivery detail not disclosed by the cited source remains source not stated; it is not inferred from product imagery or marketing language.
en.painPointsSolved: AMP targets the collaboration gap in single-player AI: a personal agent completes work without clear ownership, team visibility, reusable context, or auditable authority. Putting people and agents in one workspace reduces copy-paste and status chasing; making service accounts and non-human identities explicit reduces the cost of answering who changed a document and what it could see. It does not remove misunderstanding, permission errors, or cross-tool semantic loss. Any price, version, region, interface, battery, success rate, privacy, or delivery detail not disclosed by the cited source remains source not stated; it is not inferred from product imagery or marketing language.
en.userVoice: Public evidence is currently Atlassian's article and platform documentation. This run found no sufficient long-term customer testing to show that agent cursors, identity panels, human checkpoints, and cross-tool write-back remain smooth in complex projects. AMP is an official direction and rollout statement, not a general success rate or satisfaction claim. Any price, version, region, interface, battery, success rate, privacy, or delivery detail not disclosed by the cited source remains source not stated; it is not inferred from product imagery or marketing language.
en.newTech: The move is not a single model but the combination of agent identity, shared presence, Teamwork Graph context, permission inheritance, local-session bridging, and audit as one multiplayer protocol. Agent output becomes attributable, permissioned, and lifecycle-managed team activity rather than a chat transcript, making revocation, audit, version tracking, and accountability first-class product objects. Any price, version, region, interface, battery, success rate, privacy, or delivery detail not disclosed by the cited source remains source not stated; it is not inferred from product imagery or marketing language.
en.availability: Atlassian announced that AMP begins rollout and listed Jira, Confluence, Rovo, MCP, Artifacts, and Agent Sessions as related platform entry points. The cited material does not state the full region, plan, admin switches, formal API documentation, third-party client matrix, or GA schedule; the actual account and product version remain the source of truth. Any price, version, region, interface, battery, success rate, privacy, or delivery detail not disclosed by the cited source remains source not stated; it is not inferred from product imagery or marketing language.
en.limitsOrUnknowns: Open questions include administrator controls for agent identity, cross-organisation work, offline local-session sync, Figma and IDE permissions, sensitive-document summarisation boundaries, generated content after revocation, graph errors, agent conflicts, and checkpoint frequency. Making everything visible can also create notification noise that makes genuine takeover moments harder to spot. Any price, version, region, interface, battery, success rate, privacy, or delivery detail not disclosed by the cited source remains source not stated; it is not inferred from product imagery or marketing language.
en.productVerdict: AMP is a concrete developer surface worth tracking as infrastructure for team agents. Verdict: it moves agents from personal productivity add-ons into a shared accountability space and fills identity, context, and audit gaps. The next gate is proving that teams are not buried in state and that users can understand, edit, pause, and revoke agent behaviour from one work surface. A credible rollout also needs visible permission boundaries, reversible actions, durable activity history, and a clear handoff when an agent reaches an uncertain or high-impact decision. Those interaction details will determine whether multiplayer agents feel like accountable colleagues or opaque automation attached to a busy project. candidates.enHeadline: OpenAI Decisions API turns model judgement into a callable selector
candidates.zhFact: OpenAI Developer Community 公告称 Decisions API 已面向所有开发者公测。它接受文本和图像输入，输出 predicates（真假概率）、choices（固定选项与 confidence）或 scores（按数值区间评估），目标是让应用近实时选择模型、工具或动作。公告声称相对 GPT-6 Luna 经 Responses API 可快至 10 倍；这属于官方公告口径，不能当作所有输入的实测延迟。
candidates.enFact: An OpenAI Developer Community announcement says the Decisions API is in public beta for all developers. It accepts text and image inputs and returns predicates with probabilities, choices from a fixed set with confidence, or scores against a numeric range, allowing an application to select a model, tool, or action near real time. The announcement claims up to 10x faster decisions than GPT-6 Luna through the Responses API; that is an announcement claim, not a latency result for every input.
candidates.zhValue: 这条 API 把许多产品里的‘分类后决定下一步’从长文本生成链里抽出来：图片审核可以输出是否符合规则，路由器可以从固定工具集合选一个动作，工作流可以把输入打分后决定升级、拒绝或交给人工。对 HCI，重要变化是模型判断成为可观察的系统状态，而不是藏在一段自然语言解释里。
candidates.enValue: The API extracts a common product step—classify, then decide what happens next—from a long-form generation chain. Image moderation can return whether a rule is met, a router can choose one action from a fixed tool set, and a workflow can score an input before escalating, rejecting, or handing it to a person. For HCI, the important change is that model judgement becomes an observable system state rather than a decision hidden inside prose.
candidates.zhImplication: 验收要看固定选项是否真的限制了动作空间、confidence 低时是否转人工、评分标准是否可解释、图像输入是否保留审计、超时和无缓存时用户能否知道成本与延迟。开发者社区当天讨论了输入 token 缓存和 3D 游戏图像测试的延迟，说明真实摩擦会落在计费、网络与边界条件，而不是 API 名称本身。
candidates.enImplication: Acceptance should test whether fixed choices really constrain the action space, whether low confidence routes to a human, whether a score rubric is explainable, whether image inputs remain auditable, and whether timeout or no-cache conditions expose cost and latency. Same-day developer discussion raised input-token caching and image latency in a 3D-game test, showing that real friction will sit in billing, network, and edge cases rather than the API name.

en.productName: Decisions API is a developer-facing judgement surface on the OpenAI API, shown in a public-beta announcement dated October 2026. It is not a chat UI: it turns text or image inputs into a predicate, choice, or score that an application can use to select the next model, tool, action, or human path. Any price, version, region, interface, battery, success rate, privacy, or delivery detail not disclosed by the cited source remains source not stated; it is not inferred from product imagery or marketing language.
en.productType: The product is a low-latency decision API and developer surface. It extracts fixed-choice selection, probability estimation, and numeric scoring from a general Responses flow for routing, moderation, escalation, and tool-selection nodes. Model version, region, price, quota, SDK version, and formal SLA are not fully described in the cited announcement. Any price, version, region, interface, battery, success rate, privacy, or delivery detail not disclosed by the cited source remains source not stated; it is not inferred from product imagery or marketing language.
en.interactionFlow: An application submits text or an image plus a condition, fixed option set, or scoring range. The API returns predicate probabilities, a choice with confidence, or a score. Application code then selects the next step: call a tool, escalate to a person, block a submission, switch models, or continue. Low confidence, timeout, indeterminate output, and human override should be explicit states rather than silently converted into an ordinary answer. Any price, version, region, interface, battery, success rate, privacy, or delivery detail not disclosed by the cited source remains source not stated; it is not inferred from product imagery or marketing language.
en.specsOrStack: The announcement discloses text and image inputs, three output types, and an official comparison claim of up to 10x faster decisions than GPT-6 Luna through the Responses API. It does not fully state model version, maximum input, caching, billing unit, region, throughput, structured-schema details, SDK, logging, retention, or rate limits; these remain source not stated. Any price, version, region, interface, battery, success rate, privacy, or delivery detail not disclosed by the cited source remains source not stated; it is not inferred from product imagery or marketing language.
en.useCases: Concrete cases include deciding whether an image meets a site rule, selecting one action from a fixed tool set, scoring a ticket or document against a rubric, deciding whether to escalate for human review, selecting the next action in a game or robotic vision loop, and routing an input to a cheaper model, frontier model, or specialised tool. A fixed option set constrains actions but does not make the judgement correct. Any price, version, region, interface, battery, success rate, privacy, or delivery detail not disclosed by the cited source remains source not stated; it is not inferred from product imagery or marketing language.
en.painPointsSolved: It addresses the verbosity, unpredictability, and audit cost of using a general generation API at routing or classification nodes. A developer can request an enum-like action and confidence instead of parsing prose about which tool to use, and can store the scoring rubric as structured data. The trade-off is moving rubric, choice, and fallback responsibility into product design; a fast wrong classification can trigger a fast wrong action. Any price, version, region, interface, battery, success rate, privacy, or delivery detail not disclosed by the cited source remains source not stated; it is not inferred from product imagery or marketing language.
en.userVoice: After the announcement, developers discussed whether input tokens are cached, a personal image test that reported about 0.8 seconds on a 3 Mbps connection, and whether choice questions fit probability prediction. These are community friction and individual experiments, not an official SLA. They still point to caching, cost, network variance, confidence explanation, and calibration as acceptance requirements. Any price, version, region, interface, battery, success rate, privacy, or delivery detail not disclosed by the cited source remains source not stated; it is not inferred from product imagery or marketing language.
en.newTech: The technical move is treating a model as a composable decision function rather than asking it to generate a long response every time. Predicates, choices, and scores map to rule judgement, action selection, and continuous evaluation, allowing a model to sit inside an existing state machine, workflow, tool router, or approval chain. It is closer to an AI-native control primitive than a new chat surface. Any price, version, region, interface, battery, success rate, privacy, or delivery detail not disclosed by the cited source remains source not stated; it is not inferred from product imagery or marketing language.
en.availability: The OpenAI Developer Community announcement says the Decisions API is available to all developers in public beta and provides a try-it entry point. Formal documentation, pricing, regions, enterprise support, production limits, and compatibility commitments are not fully disclosed in the cited surface. Products using it for consequential actions still need schema validation, retries, human fallback, and audit. Any price, version, region, interface, battery, success rate, privacy, or delivery detail not disclosed by the cited source remains source not stated; it is not inferred from product imagery or marketing language.
en.limitsOrUnknowns: Open questions include probability calibration, confidence semantics, visual errors in complex scenes, no-cache cost, rate limits, input retention, prompt injection, schema drift, model upgrades, cross-region latency, and low-confidence fallback. An 'up to 10x' claim does not replace benchmarking on real load, network, and image size. Any price, version, region, interface, battery, success rate, privacy, or delivery detail not disclosed by the cited source remains source not stated; it is not inferred from product imagery or marketing language.
en.productVerdict: Decisions API is a concrete developer surface whose value is making next-step judgement measurable, constrained, and auditable. Verdict: it may remove a natural-language parsing layer from agent workflows, but speed becomes reliable product value only when confidence, cost, human takeover, and version changes are legible. Any price, version, region, interface, battery, success rate, privacy, or delivery detail not disclosed by the cited source remains source not stated; it is not inferred from product imagery or marketing language.

event.summaryZh: OpenAI Developer Community 公告称 Decisions API 已面向所有开发者公测。它接受文本和图像输入，输出 predicates（真假概率）、choices（固定选项与 confidence）或 scores（按数值区间评估），目标是让应用近实时选择模型、工具或动作。公告声称相对 GPT-6 Luna 经 Responses API 可快至 10 倍；这属于官方公告口径，不能当作所有输入的实测延迟。
event.summaryEn: An OpenAI Developer Community announcement says the Decisions API is in public beta for all developers. It accepts text and image inputs and returns predicates with probabilities, choices from a fixed set with confidence, or scores against a numeric range, allowing an application to select a model, tool, or action near real time. The announcement claims up to 10x faster decisions than GPT-6 Luna through the Responses API; that is an announcement claim, not a latency result for every input.
event.deltaZh: 这条 API 把许多产品里的‘分类后决定下一步’从长文本生成链里抽出来：图片审核可以输出是否符合规则，路由器可以从固定工具集合选一个动作，工作流可以把输入打分后决定升级、拒绝或交给人工。对 HCI，重要变化是模型判断成为可观察的系统状态，而不是藏在一段自然语言解释里。
event.deltaEn: The API extracts a common product step—classify, then decide what happens next—from a long-form generation chain. Image moderation can return whether a rule is met, a router can choose one action from a fixed tool set, and a workflow can score an input before escalating, rejecting, or handing it to a person. For HCI, the important change is that model judgement becomes an observable system state rather than a decision hidden inside prose.

candidates.enHeadline: femtoAI opens an SPU developer surface for smaller edge-AI systems
candidates.zhFact: femtoAI 10 月 7 日宣布开发者社区开放，提供 Sparse Processing Unit（SPU）芯片评估套件、压缩模型、编译器与 Sparsity Studio。公司称其稀疏神经网络和模型压缩可以带来 10 倍更低功耗与 10 倍更小内存占用，并举出 Whisper 压缩、local voice commands、穿戴、家电、智能眼镜与机器人作为方向。该数字仍是公司声明。
candidates.enFact: On October 7, femtoAI announced open access to its developer community with an SPU chip evaluation kit, compressed models, a compiler, and Sparsity Studio. The company says its sparse neural networks and model compression can deliver 10x lower power draw and a 10x smaller memory footprint, citing compressed Whisper, local voice commands, wearables, appliances, smart glasses, and robotics as directions. The figures remain company claims.
candidates.zhValue: 这条产品信号的重点是把‘端侧 AI 太大、太热、太耗电’转成开发者可以试的工具链。评估套件让产品团队先用目标模型、语音和传感任务评估内存与功耗，再决定是否把 SPU 放进耳机、眼镜、家居或机器人。它不保证产品自动拥有更好的识别率，也不等于一块评估板已经变成可量产的终端。
candidates.enValue: The product signal is about turning the edge-AI problem—too large, hot, and power-hungry—into a toolchain developers can try. The evaluation kit lets a product team test target models, voice, and sensor tasks against memory and power before deciding whether an SPU belongs in earbuds, glasses, home appliances, or a robot. It does not guarantee better recognition and does not make an evaluation board a mass-produced device.
candidates.zhImplication: 验收要把稀疏化前后的模型输出、唤醒率、误触发、功耗曲线、编译失败、算子覆盖、模型更新和弱网/离线降级一起测。对穿戴产品，省下的内存应转成更长待机或更快反馈，而不是被新的传感器和网络任务吃掉；对用户，最终要能感知为少充电、少等待、少上传，而不是看见一个 SPU 名词。
candidates.enImplication: Acceptance should measure model output, wake rate, false triggers, power curves, compiler failures, operator coverage, model updates, and weak-network or offline degradation before and after sparsification. In wearables, saved memory should become longer standby or faster feedback rather than being consumed by new sensors and network tasks. The user should feel fewer charges, less waiting, and less uploading—not see an SPU acronym.

event.deltaEn: The product signal is about turning the edge-AI problem—too large, hot, and power-hungry—into a toolchain developers can try.
